picks.editorial_note: MIT's Regina Barzilay and Jim Collins won the 2026 Pritzker Prize for AI in Science, the field's top honor, for pioneering AI-driven antibiotic discovery that has already identified novel compounds — a landmark validation of AI's power to accelerate drug discovery against rising antimicrobial resistance.
picks.title: Regina Barzilay and Jim Collins win Pritzker Prize for AI and Science Research Excellence for work in AI-enabled antibiotic discovery

picks.editorial_note: Nebraska will lead cybersecurity for FabAID, a five-year $24.5M NSF national infrastructure project, underscoring growing federal investment in securing the computing fabric that underpins AI-driven scientific research nationwide.
picks.title: University to lead cybersecurity for national Fabric for AI-Driven Science project

picks.editorial_note: Boston University joined a $39.5M ARPA-H consortium with Philips, Johns Hopkins, and Weill Cornell to build AI-enabled robotic catheters for remote stroke treatment, a major cross-sector bet on AI closing care gaps in time-critical medicine.
picks.title: Brink Bites: Robotic Stroke Surgery, Curbing Junk Food Sales, and American Attitudes On Data Center Construction

picks.editorial_note: Anthropic's pledge of up to 5% of its equity (potentially $100 billion) alongside SpaceX's giveaways raises major questions about who benefits from AI windfalls — a scale of wealth redistribution with real policy implications that academics are now publicly scrutinizing.
picks.title: Billions in SpaceX, Anthropic Stock Pledged to the Public. Who Benefits? - Georgetown University

picks.editorial_note: HKUST and HSBC signed a strategic framework to advance AI and financial innovation through a new joint institute, deepening a near-three-decade relationship and signaling how major banks are formalizing ties with universities to shape applied AI research.
picks.title: HKUST and HSBC Forge Strategic Partnership to Advance AI, Emerging Technologies and Financial Innovation
picks.university: Hong Kong Univ. of Science and Technology

picks.editorial_note: Tel Aviv University and Stanford researchers showed AI models can learn general predictive skills purely from self-generated synthetic data, a potentially significant breakthrough for reducing AI's dependence on scarce real-world training data.
picks.title: AI Learns to Predict the World Without Ever Seeing It

picks.editorial_note: HKUST launched a HK$100 million RAISe+ fund for research commercialization alongside new robotics work, reflecting a substantial institutional bet on turning AI research into deployable technology and startups.
picks.title: October Research & Innovation Roundup
picks.university: Hong Kong Univ. of Science and Technology

picks.editorial_note: A $3.2M NIH-funded ASU project combining deep learning with retinal imaging and blood biomarkers could enable low-cost, early screening for preclinical Alzheimer's disease, with major implications for early intervention at scale.
picks.title: What the eye may reveal about Alzheimer’s

picks.editorial_note: UW-led research found leading AI models from Google and OpenAI are biased against certain English accents in evaluating interviews and tests, a fairness finding with direct implications for AI deployment in hiring and education policy.
picks.title: Leading AI models are biased against certain accents when scoring interviews, presentations and tests | UW News

picks.editorial_note: Georgia State's Dong Hye Ye earned an NSF CAREER Award to develop vision-language AI combining medical imaging with clinical text, recognizing promising early-career work at the intersection of AI and diagnostic medicine.
picks.title: Georgia State Computer Science Professor Earns National Science Foundation Early Career Award
